HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. KOREAN FACES on everyone in frame: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, blue, grey or green, never the whole eyeball painted solid black); a low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European nose. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. INTIMATE night interior, low three-quarter from the packed-earth floor. ONE DEVICE: a heavy timber chair on axis, FIVE straight Korean ring-pommel swords hung on the wall behind it like a dark comb. SMALL warm Pyongyang timber room — red pillars, lime plaster, one iron lamp on the floor at the LEFT of the lens raking up. OLD Yeon Gesomun (LEFT of the sheet, iron-grey hair, grey beard, NEVER the young black-haired face) sits the chair in a charcoal inner robe and red sash, NO armor, NO five swords on his back, sitting UP, glaring, dying and refusing to lie down. Three sons standing in the midground, ONE OF EACH, never cloned: SECOND = Namseng closest to the chair (tight bun, two short temple-strands, neat goatee, rigid, charcoal court po, red scarf knot, NO helm, NO long hair). THIRD = Namgun (LONG loose black hair past the shoulders, fuller beard, louder stance). FOURTH = Namsan (rounder younger face, looking aside, NO helm). #d0362f as the lamp key on old Yeon's cheek, not a glow. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = gesomun, SECOND face = namseng, THIRD face = namgun, FOURTH face = namsan. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces). BOTTOM ROW: the only sword design. KOREAN FACES on every person, named or extra: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a small catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, honey, gold, blue, grey, green or purple). Never paint the entire eyeball solid black. A low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European, Roman or Persian nose. East Asian bone: single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair. Never Western, Latin, or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes. YEON GESOMUN — Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Now: Last years (ch_yeon_gesomun_old): iron-grey hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord, grey-streaked beard, heavier jowls, same glare; still in red-wing Goguryeo lamellar and a red cape. Colour #d0362f. YEON NAMSENG — Look: Gesomun's eldest: a tight high bun, TWO short loose strands at the temples, a neat goatee and thin moustache, a rigid square jaw, no long hair. Never Namgun's shoulder-length hair. Never Namsan's helm. Dress: Goguryeo steel lamellar with a RED scarf knot at the throat and a red sash; one crow-ring sword. In 666–668, when he rides west: a TANG vermilion court coat over steel, no red-wing flaps, no Goguryeo scarf. Colour #c25a4e. YEON NAMGUN — Look: Gesomun's second: LONG loose black hair past the shoulders, a fuller beard covering the jaw, wilder heavier brows than Namseng, a bow-case on his back. Never Namseng's short temple-strands. Never Namsan's helm. Dress: Goguryeo steel lamellar with red laces, a gold square belt-plate, a red wrap at the hip, one crow-ring sword and a strung bow. Colour #9e3b32. YEON NAMSAN — Look: Gesomun's youngest: a rounder shorter face, a small goatee, eyes that look aside or down. Out of battle: a plain topknot, no helm. On the wall and in the field: a black rounded helm with a RED horsehair plume and a gold disc on the brow (his portrait helm). Dress: Goguryeo steel lamellar, a red cloak tied at the throat, a red sash; a polearm or one crow-ring sword. He is the one who walks out with the white banner. Colour #d4776a. Any sword is the ancient straight Korean ring-pommel dao: a small iron ring pommel, a short wrapped grip, a thin metal band and NO hand guard, a perfectly straight blade — never a katana, never a tsuba. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
